input.quote: Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf a worldwide, non-exclusive right during the subscription term to access and use the hosted Services and documentation for their internal business purposes and to provide services to Customer.
input.rationale: Section 13 meets the preferred position in full, so no redline is warranted. (1)-(2) The subscription grant in 13.1 expressly extends to Customer's Affiliates and to "contractors acting on their behalf" (no written-notice condition needed), and 13.2 likewise covers Affiliates and permits contractors to support paid-up material. (3)-(4) Paid-up and embedded software/Vendor Technology is licensed on a "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid" basis under 13.2, and 10.1 confirms paid-up licence rights survive expiry or termination. (5) The subscription licence is not revocable or suspendable at will: 13.3 permits revocation or suspension only "during a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure." (6) 13.3 allows Customer to transfer licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24, and 24.1 permits assignment without Vendor consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets, with 24.4 barring Vendor from terminating, repricing, or reducing service on Customer's change of control. The grant is not styled "non-transferable" or "revocable", so the walk-away scenario does not arise. This sits above the fallback at the preferred level.
